subject: Post-call: Finlytics POC — flow control, auth & idempotency
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finlytics.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended architecture safeguards (Auth, routing, 429s)

Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete list of next steps so we can scope the Finlytics POC (focus: embedded reranker, structured outputs, and resilient client behavior under quota pressure).

High-level notes
- Goal: integrate Redwood embeddings + reranker into your search pipeline for the risk scoring UI; POC target = 100k queries/day with 95th percentile latency target of 600ms for interactive flows.
- Primary concerns you raised: auth/key rotation, bursty traffic from batch re-ranks, and how clients should handle 429s without double-applying scoring updates.

Recommended architecture and mitigations
1) SDK & auth
   - Use the Redwood SDK for initial POC (we'll share a pinned version). SDK supports short-lived API keys via your KMS; rotate keys every 24 hours during the POC to validate rotation flows.
   - Deploy a small proxy in your VPC to centralize key usage and token refresh; this prevents leaking long-lived keys in client apps.

2) Routing & capacity tiers
   - Route interactive scoring to a low-latency pool (dedicated), and batch re-ranks to a throughput-optimized pool.
   - Use request metadata to set priority: header X-Redwood-Priority: interactive|batch. The runtime will prefer interactive capacity when provided.

3) Rate limiting, quotas, and graceful degradation
   - Surface rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset) to your callers and replenish caches every 1s.
   - Implement a client-side token bucket with a small local queue and adaptive concurrency to smooth bursty spikes from batch jobs.

4) Retries & idempotency (critical for scoring correctness)
   - All mutating scorer calls (e.g., submit-score) MUST include an idempotency-key generated by the client (UUIDv4) and persisted until a terminal response.
   - For 429s: apply exponential backoff with full jitter (base 200ms, cap 30s). Retry only once for interactive flows; for batch jobs allow configurable retry budget.
   - Use request_id in logs for tracing: Redwood will echo back X-Request-Id for each processed request. Persist mapping of client idempotency-key -> request_id for audit.

5) Structured output & tool calling
   - For structured reprs we recommend v2 schema (schema descriptor attached). If a tool-call times out, return the last-safe fallback: cached candidate list and a passive "retry in background" process that updates the UI asynchronously.

6) Embeddings & reranker tips
   - Keep embedding requests batched (up to 64 items) to improve throughput and lower per-embedding cost; for tight-latency interactive flows, fall back to single-item requests.
   - For rerankers, implement a fallback scoring heuristic (TF-IDF + small ML model) when the reranker service returns 429/503 to avoid blanking results. Also rate-limit per-user to avoid hot keys.

Next steps (concrete)
- Redwood: share SDK tarball and an example proxy config by end of week (attaching diagram + scope).
- Finlytics: confirm which flows are interactive vs. batch and share expected per-minute concurrency numbers.
- Schedule a 45-min POC kickoff to agree on observability and SLAs (suggest Thu 7/17 10am PT).

Attachments: Finlytics POC scope (pdf), proposed integration diagram (png).

If that looks right I'll open a HubSpot POC deal and add the kickoff invite.

—
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finlytics.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended architecture safeguards (Auth, routing, 429s)

Thanks Naomi — this is excellent and covers our concerns. Two quick clarifications: 
1) For idempotency keys, do you recommend storing the mapping client-side only, or should we persist on our backend for at-least-once semantics?
2) Our batch re-ranker runs as a cron that can spike to 400 concurrent requests for a 10-minute window. Will your suggested token-bucket handle that, or do you recommend using server-side queuing?

Happy to take the kickoff on Thu 7/17 10am PT — tentatively accepted.

—
Alex Torres
Head of Search, Finlytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finlytics.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended architecture safeguards (Auth, routing, 429s)

Alex — short answers:
- Persist idempotency-key mapping in your backend for any operation that must be "exactly-once" from the application perspective (scoring writes, billing events). Client-only persistence is acceptable for ephemeral interactive flows where duplicate scoring is low-impact.
- For the batch spike: combine client-side token buckets with a small server-side FIFO queue (we can provide an open-source queue helper) and use weighted backoff to shed load. The idea: accept requests at your proxy up to a soft limit and return 202 Accepted + retry-after when the queue is full, rather than 429-ing origin clients.

I'll attach a short checklist for the kickoff with code snippets (we'll push to the POC Drive folder).

—
Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
